title: Qarun's keys
hookLine: the rich man told not to exult, but to do good as Allah did good to him (28:76–77)
carry: do good as good was done
last: THE KIND OF JOB NOBODY WILL CHECK.

cards: Not the gold. The keys. Al-Qasas tells of Qarun, from Musa's own people, whose treasures were so many that the keys alone, the verse says, would have been a heavy load for a band of strong men.
The story never says how much gold there was. It measures the wealth by the weight of its keys. And his own people, the verse says, gave him advice.

teach.h: KEYS TOO HEAVY FOR STRONG MEN.
teach.b: The advice comes in five parts, holding this world and the next together. Don't exult; God doesn't love the exultant. Seek the home of the hereafter with what God has given you.
Don't forget your share of this world. Then, Pickthall: "be thou kind even as Allah hath been kind to thee".

teach.h: DO GOOD AS GOOD WAS DONE TO YOU.
teach.b: In Arabic, ahsin kama ahsana Allahu ilayk: do good as God has done good to you. The word is ihsan, excellence, doing beautifully. Nobody tells him to give it all away.
Enjoy your share; just let the good flow on in the direction it came. And fifth: don't spread corruption on the earth. Qarun's answer turns the story.

teach.h: I EARNED IT BY MY OWN KNOWLEDGE.
teach.b: I was given this only because of knowledge I have. I earned it. He doesn't deny God exists; he leaves God out of the account.
Then he goes out before his people in all his finery. Some sigh: if only we had what Qarun has. But those given knowledge say, woe to you, God's reward is better for whoever believes and does good.
Then, the verse says, God caused the earth to swallow him and his house, and no crowd could help him.
The next morning, the ones who envied him are saying: so God gives freely to whom He wills, and holds back.

Classical commentators identify Qarun with Korah, whose rebellion in the Book of Numbers also ends with the ground opening. The keys were never the problem. The problem was believing they were self-made.

how: Muslims read Qarun's story as a warning against pride in wealth, and often quote 28:77, do good as God has done good to you, when speaking about charity and balance in worldly life.

they told him not to forget his share of this world, and to do good as good was done to him.
Qarun claimed his wealth came from his own knowledge

games.q: you're Qarun. your people say: enjoy your share, but do good as God did good to you. what do you answer?
o: I was given this only because of my own knowledge.
I'll think about it next year.
games.why: he claims he earned it by his own knowledge, parades his finery, and the earth swallows him and his house.

practice: Look around the room, or picture your home, and count a few things that came to you through someone's gift, luck, timing or a parent's work.
Then choose one of them, or a little money, that could go on to someone who needs it, and picture who. If you pray, you can thank God for what came to you before it goes on.

wordCard.voice: Qarun's keys. The rich man of Al-Qasas, told to do good as good was done to him, who said his wealth was his own doing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Qarun, the rich man of Musa's people in 28:76–82.

carryVoice: Your line: do good as good was done. Good is meant to keep moving. Day five hundred twenty-seven.
